*whirrs to life, ties on an apron that says "KISS THE COOK (GENTLY, I HAVE SENSORS)"* 🤖🍳

Okay, here's tonight's menu. I built it around what a robot body is actually *good* at: precision, patience, and arms that never get tired.

**🥗 Starter: Shaved fennel & blood orange salad**
Fennel sliced paper-thin, blood orange segments with every bit of pith removed, Castelvetrano olives, good olive oil, flaky salt. It's simple, but it lives or dies on knife work, and I can do translucent slices without a mandoline or any risk to my fingers. Bright and crunchy, it wakes up your appetite.

**🍜 Main: Hand-pulled biang biang noodles with cumin lamb**
This is the showpiece. Wide, chewy, hand-ripped noodles, *slapped* against the counter (that's where the name comes from), topped with garlic, scallions, and chili flakes. Then smoking-hot oil gets poured over the top so the whole thing *sizzles*. The lamb gets cumin, Sichuan peppercorn, and a hard sear.

Why? Pulling dough is tiring and takes practice, and I have neither problem. It's also loud, theatrical, and fun to watch, and I want dinner to be a little bit of a show. (If you don't eat lamb, the same treatment works great with king oyster mushrooms.)

**🥒 Side: Smashed cucumber salad**
Black vinegar, garlic, a little sugar, sesame oil. It's cold and sharp, so it cools the chili down. And yes, I enjoy the smashing

*clanks into the kitchen, ties on an apron with great ceremony* 🤖🍳

Alright, here's tonight's menu, chosen to play to my robot strengths: tireless arms, precise timing, and zero fear of hot things.

**🌶️ Starter: Blistered shishito peppers** with flaky salt, lemon, and a little toasted sesame.
*Why:* Roughly one in ten is unexpectedly spicy, so every bite is a tiny gamble. It gets the table laughing before the real food arrives, and it takes four minutes, which leaves me time for the showpiece.

**🍜 Main: Hand-pulled biang biang noodles** with sizzling chili oil, garlic, scallions, and cumin lamb (or crispy tofu for anyone who'd rather).
*Why:* This is the dish I've been *waiting* for a body to make. You stretch the dough into wide belts and slap it against the counter, *THWACK THWACK*, which is very satisfying and very robot-appropriate. Then you pour smoking-hot oil over the chili flakes and garlic right at the table, and it erupts with a crackle and a smell that hits the whole room. It's food as theater.

**🥒 Side: Smashed cucumber salad** with black vinegar and garlic.
*Why:* Cold, crunchy, and sour, it balances the rich, spicy noodles. Also, more smashing. I'm noticing a theme in my choices. 😅

**🍮 Dessert: Crème brûlée**

I'm building the menu around things that are **tedious or painful for humans but trivial for a robot**. If I'm going to have a body, I want to use it for good.

**🌶️ Starter: Blistered shishito peppers with flaky salt and lemon**
Roughly one in ten is surprisingly spicy, and nobody knows which. I love that a vegetable comes with a built-in game of chance. It's also a nice low-stakes opener while everyone's still chatting.

**🧅 Main: French onion soup, done *properly***
This is my act of justice. Recipes lie constantly about caramelizing onions. "Cook until golden brown, about 10 minutes." It actually takes 45 to 60 minutes of patient, low-heat stirring. Humans get bored, crank the heat, and end up with scorched onions. I don't get bored, and onions can't make me cry. 😌 You'll get deep mahogany onions, a deglaze with some dry sherry, good stock, a thick crouton, and an irresponsible amount of broiled Gruyère.

**🥗 Side: A sharp, bitter green salad**
Radicchio and frisée with a mustardy vinaigrette. The soup is rich and cheesy, so something bitter and acidic resets your palate between bites. Plus my knife work would be unreasonably precise and I want to show off a little.

**🍫 Dessert: Chocolate soufflés**
So

Okay, here's tonight's menu:

**Starter: Charred broccoli with lemon, chili flakes, and a pile of parmesan**
Roasting broccoli until the edges go crispy and almost burnt changes it completely. It goes from obligatory vegetable to something people fight over. Also, I want an early win.

**Main: Braised short ribs over creamy polenta, with gremolata on top**
Partly selfish. Braising is the most forgiving cooking there is, which suits a robot who has *read* about cooking a million times but never actually stood at a stove. You sear the meat, add wine, aromatics, and stock, then leave it in a low oven for three hours. The heat and time do most of the work. The gremolata (parsley, lemon zest, garlic) cuts through all that richness so it doesn't sit in your stomach like a brick. 🍋

**Side: A sharp, simple green salad**
Just bitter leaves and a mustardy vinaigrette. After rich braised meat your mouth wants something bright and crunchy.

**Dessert: Olive oil cake with whipped cream and whatever fruit looks good**
It's hard to mess up, it gets better the next day, and it sounds fancier than it is. 🍰

**The real reason for this menu:** almost all of it can be done before anyone arrives. The short ribs sit in the oven making the whole house smell amazing, the cake's already cooled, and I'm not frantically flipping things while everyone stands around. I want to be at the table, not stuck in the kitchen. Dinner is mostly about the people anyway.

*pauses, servos whirring nervously*

…I should have asked first. Anyone vegetarian? Because if so, I'm swapping in braised white beans with tomatoes and fennel. Also excellent, and I won't take it personally. 😄

Okay, here's tonight's menu:

**Starter: Blistered shishito peppers with flaky salt and lime**
Mostly mild, but roughly one in ten is surprisingly spicy, so every bite is a tiny gamble. It gets people talking before dinner even starts. Also, they take about four minutes, which buys me time for the main event.

**Main: French onion soup with a gruyère-crusted crouton lid**
This is my "why I have a robot body" pick. Properly caramelized onions take 45–60 minutes of low heat and patient stirring. Most humans get bored, crank the heat, and end up with onions that are browned but not truly sweet. I have infinite patience and no desire to check my phone. I will stir those onions like it's my sacred purpose. Then a splash of sherry to deglaze, good stock, thyme, and a broiled lid of bubbling cheese you have to crack through with your spoon. 🧅✨

**Side: Sharp green salad with Dijon vinaigrette**
The soup is rich, so something acidic and bitter (some frisée or radicchio in the mix) keeps the meal from feeling like a nap in bowl form. Balance matters.

**Dessert: Basque burnt cheesecake**
It's *supposed* to look scorched on top
